schema_notes.nodes: Entities that can appear as points on a relational map: factions, regions, institutions, characters, ideologies, bloodlines, etc.
schema_notes.links: Directional or mutual relationships between nodes: patronage, destabilization, dependency, fear, alliance, secrecy, control, etc.
schema_notes.events: Plot events that alter nodes, links, power, visibility, or public interpretation.
schema_notes.strength_scale: 1-10, where 1 is faint/minor and 10 is existential/defining.
schema_notes.power_scale: 1-10, where 1 is marginal and 10 is dominant.
schema_notes.relationship_softness: Some links, especially spiritual and aristocratic links, are affective or existential rather than contractual: belief, love, fear, devotion, family overlap, initiation, or private reliance.
schema_notes.supernatural_power_scale: 1-10, where 1 is minimal/rumored and 10 is overwhelming or city-shaping supernatural leverage.

nodes.name: Lyne Syndicate
nodes.legitimacy: Unofficial; protected by usefulness to Hightowns powers.
nodes.primary_goal: Preserve Hightowns dominance and security.
nodes.primary_fear: Lowtowns becoming organized, prosperous, politically unified, or otherwise able to threaten Hightowns.
nodes.public_face: Usually none. Lyne may operate through fronts, intermediaries, merchants, civic patrons, legal channels, security fronts, or rumors, but it is not generally understood as a public organization.
nodes.actual_function: Maintain pressure on Lowtowns so it stays useful, governable from above, dependent, fragmented, and non-threatening to Hightowns. Lyne is order-focused but illegal: it uses destabilization and chaos as tools against enemies, something like a deniable intelligence operation rather than a chaos cult.
nodes.moral_frame: Sees itself as illegal/extra-legal order work in service of Hightowns stability. It uses chaos tactically against enemies, but does not value chaos as an end.
nodes.notes: Best understood as a shadow membrane between Hightowns and Lowtowns: close to Hightowns, operating on Lowtowns, deniable by the official order. It is not anti-order; it is illegal order using chaos selectively.
nodes.public_knowledge: Lyne is not usually publicly known in a clear way. Knowledge of the syndicate exists through specific incidents, rumors, partial exposure, or people who have been directly touched by its operations.
nodes.lowtowns_presence: Lyne has shadow operatives and covert assets in Lowtowns, mostly unknown and deniable. They allow Lyne to influence Lowtowns while keeping the syndicate itself obscure. During the first night this presence becomes operationally relevant: Lyne watches Workmen organizing and pressures The Culture.
nodes.first_night_activity: During the first night, Lyne is watching the Workmen/emerging Workmen community network and actively working to weaken The Culture.
nodes.fortnight_activity: During the fortnight, Lyne aims to destabilize the Workmen's burgeoning guild/community structure and severely destabilize or destroy The Culture by killing/discrediting The Boss, supporting weaker gangs, and limiting resources.
nodes.strategic_style: Illegal order-preservation through deniable disruption. Chaos is a weapon, not the goal.

nodes.name: Hightowns
nodes.legitimacy: Official / dominant civic order.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain dominance, comfort, order, and distance from Lowtowns instability.
nodes.primary_fear: Lowtowns becoming politically dangerous, economically independent, or morally impossible to ignore.
nodes.public_face: Respectable governance, wealth, civic order, elite culture.
nodes.actual_function: Dominant upper social and political order benefiting from Lowtowns dependency.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely frames itself as preserving civilization, order, and stability.
nodes.notes: Not necessarily monolithic. Later this can split into Hightowns Elite, civic government, merchant houses, old families, etc. Geographically, Hightowns is roughly one-fifth of the city, but it concentrates wealth, official power, and prestige.
nodes.geographic_scale: Much smaller than Lowtowns; roughly one-fifth of the city by rough pie-chart comparison.
nodes.spatial_note: Hightowns is geographically smaller but politically/economically dominant.

nodes.name: Lowtowns
nodes.legitimacy: Socially necessary but politically suppressed.
nodes.primary_goal: Survival, stability, dignity, and possibly self-rule or protection from exploitation.
nodes.primary_fear: Continued destabilization, poverty, factional violence, dependency, and punishment for organizing.
nodes.public_face: Lower-status districts, labor base, service population, possibly criminalized or stigmatized by Hightowns narratives.
nodes.actual_function: Provides labor, services, resources, and social/economic support to Hightowns while being politically suppressed. In practice, many internal governance functions are handled by The Culture because the Council mostly abandons Lowtowns except where Hightowns interests are directly involved.
nodes.moral_frame: Not a single moral frame; likely contains competing survival logics, reformers, opportunists, gangs, families, and organizers.
nodes.notes: Should probably be broken into sub-nodes later, because 'Lowtowns' as one blob will get visually and politically mushy. The Culture currently holds primacy in Lowtowns and functions as a de facto government in the governance vacuum. Geographically, Lowtowns is much larger than Hightowns; if the city were a pie, Lowtowns would be roughly four-fifths.
nodes.geographic_scale: Much larger than Hightowns; approximately four-fifths of the city by rough pie-chart comparison.
nodes.spatial_note: Lowtowns occupies the majority of the city's geography, even though it is politically and economically subordinated.

nodes.name: The Founder Society
nodes.legitimacy: Legal, ancestral, corporate-property, and civic-traditional; rooted in founding-family status, ownership, and control of the city's real decision-making structure.
nodes.primary_goal: Preserve and expand the power of the founding families: ancestral corporate houses whose property, business, and political interests determine the direction of the city.
nodes.primary_fear: Erosion of founding-family supremacy through Lowtowns instability, council independence, foreign leverage, rival elite families, reform movements, or dilution of the founders' exclusive table.
nodes.public_face: Founding noble families, civic patrons, old property houses, business dynasties, and guardians of the city's continuity.
nodes.actual_function: The city's real government. The Founder Society decides what must happen; the Council translates those decisions into policy, administration, enforcement, and day-to-day governance.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely frames itself as the only body with the inheritance, continuity, and long-term vision to preserve the city.
nodes.notes: The Founder Society is the legal, ancestral, boardroom-like core of city power: less a social club of all aristocrats than a table of founding-family corporate dynasties. They are not day-to-day administrators; they are the people who decide the shape of the city, then make the Council operationalize it. The Founder Society is the apex of aristocratic family power, not the entire aristocracy.
nodes.membership_rules: Mostly founding families. Not all aristocrats are represented. Occasionally a non-founder family may gain enough power to sit at the table, though the founders dislike admitting such families and likely treat them as exceptional, suspect, or useful-but-inferior.
nodes.governance_role: Sets direction and decides major policy outcomes without handling ordinary administration. It tells the Council what the city will do; the Council figures out how to implement it.
scope_of_concern: business interests of the founding families
nodes.relationship_to_lowtowns: Lowtowns has been allowed to fester under illegal power structures for roughly a century because there was less profit in direct control. Now the Founder Society wants legal order and profitability through cleanup, enforcement, labor export, and resource control.
nodes.relationship_to_council: Commands or strongly directs the Council at the level of outcomes and strategic decisions; the Council handles implementation and daily running of the city.
nodes.relationship_to_broader_aristocracy: The Founder Society represents the most powerful founding families, not all aristocratic families. There are many lesser houses beneath or outside the Founder Society's table.
nodes.fortnight_and_long_run_lowtowns_plan: Create more structure in Lowtowns with an eye for profitability: choke resources of illegal Lowtowns factions, extend the Watchmen, build a prison, hire mercenaries, formalize indentured labor export to foreign powers, and eliminate Culture/other gangs/Black Hare as autonomous illegal structures.

nodes.name: The Council
nodes.legitimacy: Formal legal government and administrative authority; publicly understood as the body that runs the city.
nodes.primary_goal: Keep the city functioning, maintain civic order, manage administration, and protect the stability of the existing Hightowns-favored system.
nodes.primary_fear: Citywide breakdown, Lowtowns unrest spilling upward, public loss of legitimacy, or being forced into visible responsibility for Founder Society decisions.
nodes.public_face: Official government, city administration, legal authority, public decision-making body.
nodes.actual_function: Runs the city day to day with a strong bias toward Hightowns interests. The Council has administrative agency, but the Founder Society can and does tell it what to do when founder-family interests are materially affected.
nodes.moral_frame: May see itself as practical governance: keeping the city running while balancing public need, Hightowns expectations, Lowtowns volatility, and Founder Society pressure.
nodes.notes: The Council is the visible city government, not just a ceremonial puppet. It runs the city, but its default tilt is toward Hightowns, and its independence narrows sharply when Founder Society interests are at stake.
nodes.relationship_to_hightowns: Institutionally biased toward Hightowns interests in ordinary governance, budgets, policing, services, and political assumptions.
nodes.relationship_to_founder_society: Normally handles governance through its own administrative machinery, but when issues matter to the founding families, the Founder Society sets the outcome and the Council implements or rationalizes it.
nodes.relationship_to_lowtowns: Manages Lowtowns as a civic problem: labor source, disorder risk, humanitarian burden, political threat, and administrative headache, often through policies that preserve Hightowns advantage.

nodes.name: Foreign Powers
nodes.legitimacy: External states, investors, military actors, trade blocs, or interventionist powers.
nodes.primary_goal: Unspecified; likely trade access, influence, leverage, extraction, alliance, or intervention.
nodes.primary_fear: Unspecified.
nodes.public_face: Diplomats, merchants, envoys, investors, military observers, treaty partners.
nodes.actual_function: External forces that the Founder Society negotiates with or uses in major business and intervention decisions.
nodes.moral_frame: Unspecified.
nodes.notes: Placeholder node added because the Founder Society has foreign intervention and business-deal concerns. Needs later detailing.

nodes.name: Spiritual Political Powers
nodes.legitimacy: Rooted in supernatural knowledge, spiritual authority, conceptual forces, ritual practice, fear, belief, love, and demonstrated power.
nodes.primary_goal: Preserve, interpret, serve, control, or embody supernatural/conceptual forces with political consequences in the City.
nodes.primary_fear: Loss of access to supernatural force, doctrinal collapse, rival practitioners, secular containment, aristocratic instrumentalization, or public unbelief turning into hostility.
nodes.public_face: Temples, cults, schools, orders, saints, mystics, ritual specialists, conceptual devotees, miracle-workers, feared houses of practice, or half-private salons.
nodes.actual_function: Acts as a network of practitioner groups whose supernatural knowledge and power give them disproportionate political weight relative to their formal institutional position.
nodes.moral_frame: Varies by group. Some may see themselves as guardians, lovers of a force, servants of truth, necessary terrors, or instruments of powers larger than politics.
nodes.relationship_to_aristocrats: Many aristocrats are tied to spiritual groups, but these ties are often less binding than founding-family structure, property, and business arrangements. Ties may be based on belief, love, fear, family participation, initiation, patronage, or private need rather than formal political contracts.
nodes.relationship_to_practitioners: Practitioners usually possess knowledge, supernatural power, or both. Their organizations tend to form around supernatural or conceptual forces with practical applications.
nodes.notes: Broad umbrella node for the City's major spiritual-political powers. Known powers so far: Fate's Paths, The Life Circle, and the unofficial Death/Dark Cult Networks. These powers are structurally different from each other: Fate's Paths is academic-consensus driven, The Life Circle is hierarchical and life-centered, and the Death/Dark Cult Networks are fragmented and officially nonexistent.

nodes.name: Practitioners
nodes.legitimacy: Derived from actual knowledge, supernatural capacity, initiation, lineage, devotion, and proximity to spiritual/conceptual forces.
nodes.primary_goal: Practice, understand, serve, wield, or survive contact with supernatural and conceptual forces.
nodes.primary_fear: Being used by aristocratic politics, hunted by rivals, severed from knowledge, spiritually consumed, or forced into public obligations.
nodes.public_face: Mystics, ritualists, specialists, clergy-adjacent figures, conceptual devotees, family initiates, private counselors, feared experts.
nodes.actual_function: Individuals or circles who carry the knowledge and power that make spiritual groups politically significant.
nodes.moral_frame: Highly variable; practitioner motives may be religious, aesthetic, fearful, loving, ambitious, inherited, coerced, or ecstatic.
nodes.notes: Many practitioners have knowledge, power, or both. Some are embedded in aristocratic families; others may be independent, feared, loved, or quietly necessary.

nodes.name: Fate's Paths
nodes.legitimacy: Academic, spiritual, and supernatural authority rooted in the study and practice of fate under the umbrella of multiple schools of thought.
nodes.primary_goal: Understand, interpret, apply, and politically navigate fate while preserving the authority and unity of Fate's Paths as the leading fate-centered spiritual power.
nodes.primary_fear: Schism, loss of consensus, rival capture of fate doctrine, misuse of individual action, damage to their spiritual connections, or outside powers exploiting school divisions.
nodes.public_face: An academic-spiritual institution in the temple ruins, organized into schools of belief and thought under the broad umbrella of fate.
nodes.actual_function: The City's most spiritually powerful and well-connected spiritual-political power, operating through internal debate, dominant consensus schools, and collective guidance on outside issues.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely sees itself as the most qualified interpreter of fate and its paths, with internal disagreement treated as part of the search for correct understanding.
nodes.notes: Located on the biggest island in the temple ruins. Structured like an academic-spiritual institution with competing schools under the umbrella of fate. Considered the most spiritually powerful and well-connected power.
nodes.location: The biggest island, centered in or around the temple ruins.
nodes.governance_structure: Academic structure with various schools of belief/thought. Schools debate under the umbrella of fate. Certain schools dominate based on consensus, and the group generally follows the guidance of the leading faction or factions on issues and outside powers.
nodes.internal_politics: Debate-driven and factional but not usually fractured. Consensus determines which schools dominate. Individual action is expected and tolerated to some degree, though the group generally acts collectively when dealing with external powers.
nodes.relationship_to_outside_powers: Generally acts as a group toward outside powers, following the guidance of whichever schools or factions currently dominate by consensus.
nodes.individual_action: Some level of individual action is expected and does happen, creating exceptions, complications, and possible political incidents.
nodes.satellite_presence: Has small satellites or unofficial presences in the city, but not a strong satellite network. Usually a couple of people and a few locations at most. Officially sanctioned external activity is rare; unofficial individuals may operate for personal, practical, or hidden reasons.
nodes.fortnight_internal_issue: Fate's Paths is moving toward a consensus pick soonish. Rue, the foreseen oracle, is expected to officially declare her initial school of thought as an adult, and her choice is assumed to sway the selection.
nodes.relationship_to_rue: Rue is the foreseen oracle. She was taught mostly by Axiomatic Path, but has not yet officially declared her school. Her declaration carries political/spiritual weight.
nodes.rue_grooming_suspicion: Some wonder whether Rue is being groomed to replace the current leader.

nodes.name: The Life Circle
nodes.legitimacy: Spiritual, practical, and conceptual authority rooted in the primacy, dominance, maintenance, and continuity of life.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain, protect, expand, and assert the dominance of life as a supernatural and conceptual force at personal, ecological, social, and macro scales.
nodes.primary_fear: Forces that diminish, corrupt, sterilize, interrupt, exploit, or subordinate life; loss of life-authority; ecological or spiritual collapse; being reduced by outsiders to mere healers.
nodes.public_face: A life-centered spiritual-political institution associated with healing, nature, living systems, vitality, continuity, and the macro-level force of life itself.
nodes.actual_function: A major spiritual-political power concerned with the dominance and maintenance of life. Healing is one major application and civic leverage point, but the institution is broader than healers.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely sees life as the primary sacred force: not just individual preservation, but the dominance, continuation, and flourishing of living systems. This can be nurturing, frightening, or politically ruthless depending on the school.
nodes.notes: Major spiritual-political power on a smaller island next to Fate's Paths. Strong but secondary to Fate's Paths in raw spiritual power and connectedness. It is not merely a healer organization: healing is a major application of a broader life-dominance doctrine.
nodes.location: A smaller island next to Fate's Paths.
nodes.governance_structure: Ruled by a selected leader who governs for life. A council chooses the leader and helps run the institution, but the council operates at the direction of the leader.
nodes.succession_model: Leader selected by council; once selected, the leader rules while they live. Leaders are generally long-lived.
nodes.internal_politics: Contains various schools of thought, but they are not treated equally. Council seats are generally determined by perceived power, spiritual strength, or connectedness rather than equal representation.
nodes.relationship_to_fates_paths: Adjacent geographically and spiritually, but generally less powerful and less connected than Fate's Paths.
nodes.relationship_to_city: Controls and provides healing as one major civic function, but its worldview and power extend beyond medicine into nature, living systems, vitality, and macro-scale life concerns.
nodes.satellite_presence: Has small satellites or unofficial presences in the city, but not a strong satellite network. Usually a couple of people and a few locations at most. Officially sanctioned external activity is rare; unofficial individuals may operate for personal, practical, or hidden reasons.
nodes.ra_threat: Ra's long-term strategy is to dethrone The Life Circle, kill or outlast its old leader, elevate a rare faction that treats death favorably, decentralize/abolish the Life Council, and fragment Life Circle power. Ra can exploit the succession uncertainty around the old leader and candidate list.
nodes.fortnight_internal_issue: Succession uncertainty: the council fears the current leader will not last and is drawing up candidates, but the decision keeps being delayed or complicated.

nodes.name: Death/Dark Cult Networks
nodes.legitimacy: Officially none. Historically delegitimized and destroyed by Fate's Paths, The Life Circle, and elements of the ruling elite, but persists through secrecy, aristocratic patronage, ruin-linked practice, and the practical impossibility of eliminating death-oriented spiritual activity entirely.
nodes.primary_goal: Varies by cult, but generally involves death, darkness, forbidden knowledge, taboo power, mortality doctrine, ruin-linked practice, and occult influence outside official recognition.
nodes.primary_fear: Open exposure, coordinated suppression, internal betrayal, growing powerful enough to trigger destruction, loss of aristocratic cover, or losing access to the death ruins.
nodes.public_face: Officially they do not exist. Publicly, the island's ruins are treated as minor and the island itself is mostly known as a playground for Hightowns elites.
nodes.actual_function: A loose, unofficial collection of death and dark cult groups operating in and around the third island and the internal death ruins after the formal death spiritual elements were destabilized and destroyed.
nodes.moral_frame: Varies widely. Some cults may pursue death for its own sake; others frame death as balance, necessary limit, plague as correction, mortality as truth, or opposition to excessive longevity and life-hoarding. Even the less murdery versions are politically radioactive.
nodes.notes: This is not a normal formal faction. It is a deniable cloud of suppressed death/dark cults centered on the third island and the internal death ruins. Its current weakness is partly an artifact of past and ongoing suppression.
nodes.location: The third island, especially the internal death ruins.
nodes.organizational_structure: Fragmented, unofficial, and deniable. Not normally treated as a single group. Individual cults or cells operate separately, with varying degrees of overlap, competition, secrecy, and patronage.
nodes.internal_politics: Not officially organized together. Some groups are more overtly death-oriented and want to do death-cult things; others are more broadly dark, mortality-focused, anti-excess-life, plague-associated, or forbidden-knowledge oriented, but still fall under the broad association of death.
nodes.relationship_to_hightowns: Many aristocrats are secretly part of or fund elements of these cult networks. Elite leisure use of the third island provides camouflage, while elite fear of scandal keeps the networks deniable.
nodes.relationship_to_city: Officially nonexistent and publicly unacceptable. Thought to be the weakest major spiritual faction, but that judgment is unreliable because they are hidden, fragmented, and periodically culled.
nodes.historical_status: The formal or openly recognized death spiritual elements were judged bad for the city by Fate's Paths, The Life Circle, and some ruling elites. They were actively destabilized and destroyed, and any open resurgence is still destroyed or suppressed.
nodes.suppression_dynamic: If death/dark groups become too open, too visible, or seem to be gaining too much power, the official spiritual-political order and ruling elites move to destabilize or destroy them again.
nodes.toleration_dynamic: Some higher-ups know the death/dark networks cannot realistically be eliminated entirely, and some believe a controlled or hidden level of their existence should be tolerated.
nodes.public_relations_problem: Some people are drawn to death/dark groups, but most people do not like them as neighbors. Their presence is more common than public institutions admit, so the city tries to squelch them, keep them minimal, or keep them hidden. Open death/dark practice is bad for tourism, migration, legitimacy, public confidence, and the city's image.
nodes.satellite_presence: Has small satellites or unofficial presences in the city, but not a strong satellite network. Usually a couple of people and a few locations at most. Officially sanctioned external activity is rare; unofficial individuals may operate for personal, practical, or hidden reasons. For death/dark groups, none of these satellites are official; if they became public, the powers that be would likely eliminate them.
nodes.fortnight_ra_alignment: During the fortnight, parts of the death/dark cult networks are loosely connected under Ra, whose current focus is more Hightowns than Lowtowns: Founders, aristocratic heads, and Fate's Paths are primary early targets.
nodes.internal_betrayal_risk: Ra intends to kill some death-cult-aligned Founders/aristocrats anyway and has not told relevant death cult leaders.
nodes.ra_long_term_reversal_plan: Ra wants to reverse the historical pattern: death cults unified under her leadership, while The Life Circle is fragmented and broken apart like death cults were.

nodes.name: Fate's Paths Schools
nodes.legitimacy: Derived from scholarly/spiritual doctrine, debate, consensus, and demonstrated insight into fate.
nodes.primary_goal: Advance competing interpretations of fate while remaining under the broader institutional umbrella of Fate's Paths.
nodes.primary_fear: Being marginalized by consensus, causing schism, being proven spiritually wrong, or having outsiders manipulate internal divisions.
nodes.public_face: Schools of thought, doctrine, interpretation, and practice.
nodes.actual_function: Internal schools debate fate doctrine; dominant schools guide collective action when consensus forms.
nodes.moral_frame: Each school likely believes it has the truest or most useful understanding of fate.
nodes.notes: Placeholder for later named schools within Fate's Paths.

nodes.name: Life Circle Leader
nodes.legitimacy: Selected by the Life Circle council and then rules for life.
nodes.primary_goal: Direct the Life Circle, preserve its authority, and guide life-centered policy and healing practice.
nodes.primary_fear: Weak legitimacy, council fracture, succession crisis, or failure to preserve life and authority.
nodes.public_face: The selected leader of the Life Circle; generally long-lived.
nodes.actual_function: Supreme internal authority once chosen, with the council operating under their direction.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely framed as stewardship of life through singular leadership.
nodes.notes: Leaders generally live a long time, making succession infrequent and therefore politically significant.

nodes.name: Life Circle Council
nodes.legitimacy: Internal governing body that selects the leader and helps run the institution.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain Life Circle institutional continuity and council influence through succession management.
nodes.primary_fear: Choosing a weak leader, loss of council influence, internal imbalance, or declining healing/spiritual authority.
nodes.public_face: Senior governing body of The Life Circle.
nodes.actual_function: Selects the leader and manages institutional affairs, but ultimately acts under the authority of the chosen leader.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely justifies unequal representation as practical recognition of real power, spiritual force, and connection.
nodes.notes: Seats are generally determined by perceived power, spiritual force, or connectedness, not equal representation.
nodes.fortnight_goal: Draw up and agree on a candidate list for replacing the current Life Circle leader before he dies or the succession becomes unstable.
nodes.succession_fear: The current leader may not last, but if the council does not pick someone he prefers, he will not retire and they may have to wait for him to die.
nodes.candidate_selection_preference: Generally prefers candidates with high supernatural power who are aligned with the council.
nodes.delay_problem: Somehow the decision keeps being delayed or running into issues.

nodes.name: Life Circle Schools
nodes.legitimacy: Schools of life-centered thought and practice within The Life Circle.
nodes.primary_goal: Advance particular understandings of life, nature, vitality, healing, continuity, and the dominance of living systems within the institution.
nodes.primary_fear: Marginalization, weak representation, and exclusion from the council hierarchy.
nodes.public_face: Different schools of life-centered thought, not limited to healing.
nodes.actual_function: Internal schools exist, but unlike Fate's Paths, they are not treated equally and do not appear to govern primarily through broad consensus.
nodes.moral_frame: Varies by school. Some may be nurturing, some ecological, some survivalist, some expansionist, some deeply unsettling in their devotion to life as dominance.
nodes.notes: Internal schools matter, but status and access are shaped by hierarchy more than equal debate. Schools are broader than healer schools. Some factions or schools may also be light-based, but in a specifically life-connected sense rather than as a separate standalone light faction tradition.

nodes.name: Third Island and Death Ruins
nodes.legitimacy: Officially treated as a site of minor importance with unknown ruins; socially used as an elite leisure/play space.
nodes.primary_goal: N/A
nodes.primary_fear: N/A
nodes.public_face: A mostly low-significance island with ruins of uncertain importance, often used as a playground for the Hightowns elite.
nodes.actual_function: Cover location for unofficial death/dark cult activity and the site of the internal death ruins.
nodes.moral_frame: N/A
nodes.notes: The ruins are officially considered of small importance, which makes the island politically invisible in a useful way.

nodes.name: Anti-Death Spiritual Policy
nodes.legitimacy: Backed by Fate's Paths, The Life Circle, and elements of the ruling elite as a civic safety, stability, and legitimacy measure.
nodes.primary_goal: Prevent death/dark spiritual factions from becoming open, powerful, respectable, or publicly influential in the city.
nodes.primary_fear: Death cult resurgence, plague ideology, anti-longevity politics, public panic, reputational damage, tourism collapse, or spiritual destabilization.
nodes.public_face: Public order, anti-cult policy, civic safety, protection against dangerous spiritual practices.
nodes.actual_function: A shared formal and informal consensus that death spiritual elements are bad for the city and must be destroyed or destabilized if they become visible or powerful.
nodes.moral_frame: The city cannot safely or respectably permit open death cult power.
nodes.notes: This is not necessarily one written law; it may be a durable shared policy consensus across spiritual and ruling powers.

nodes.name: The Culture
nodes.legitimacy: Criminal by Council/Hightowns standards, but functionally legitimate to many in Lowtowns because it provides order, protection, employment, enforcement, and governance where the Council mostly abandons them.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain Culture primacy and the old Boss's order while uncovering/eliminating Lyne from Lowtowns, insulating Lowtowns from Hightowns aggression, and drawing the Workmen into a more formal Lowtowns/Culture-aligned structure.
nodes.primary_fear: Lyne remaining hidden, Hightowns legal/security aggression breaking Lowtowns autonomy, Workmen being captured by Hightowns interests, regional gang rebellion, or The Boss failing the old Boss's legacy.
nodes.public_face: Dominant Lowtowns gang/criminal organization; protectors, enforcers, employers, and violent order-makers depending on who is speaking.
nodes.actual_function: The most powerful faction in Lowtowns and a de facto government in areas neglected by the Council. It holds the largest territory, but even outside its territory it has primacy: it can move, operate, and correct gangs across Lowtowns.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely sees itself as necessary Lowtowns order: criminal to Hightowns, but protective and principled compared to chaos, exploitation, Lyne manipulation, or Council abandonment.
nodes.relationship_to_lowtowns: Holds primacy in Lowtowns and functions as local government in many places, especially where official governance is absent or extractive.
nodes.relationship_to_council: Criminal by Council standards. Council mostly abandons Lowtowns except where Lowtowns touches Hightowns interests, mines/manufacturing, rent, or vice/black market flows that affect Hightowns.
nodes.relationship_to_lyne: The Culture wants to uncover Lyne, expose or understand its hidden Lowtowns presence, and eliminate Lyne influence from Lowtowns.
nodes.notes: The Culture should be mapped as both territorial and supra-territorial: it owns the largest territory but also functions as the correcting authority over Lowtowns gangs generally. Its primacy is a fifty-year settlement created by the old Boss.
nodes.territorial_status: Holds the largest territory in Lowtowns, but its authority extends beyond its own territory.
nodes.jurisdictional_reach: The Culture can move through other gangs' territories, operate there at will, and correct gangs that challenge its primacy or violate Culture principles/order.
nodes.historical_duration: Approximately 50 years of recognized Lowtowns primacy since the old Boss established the structure.
nodes.founding_history: The old Boss created the current power structure by going to war with the gangs for control and establishing Culture primacy across Lowtowns.
nodes.stability_history: There have been small rebellions, shifts, and changes over the past 50 years, but nothing that seriously threatened the overall power structure.
current_goals: insulate Lowtowns from general Hightowns aggression
make the Workmen more formally linked to The Culture
shift Workmen focus more toward Lowtowns than service to Hightowns
preserve Culture dominance and the old Boss's fifty-year order
nodes.relationship_to_workmen: The Culture wants the Workmen to become more formally linked to Culture and more focused on Lowtowns than Hightowns. This does not necessarily require ending Workmen neutrality; the harder problem is the Workmen network's lack of formal structure/representation.
nodes.relationship_to_hightowns: The Culture seeks to insulate Lowtowns from Hightowns aggression, extraction, and manipulation while maintaining its own primacy in Lowtowns.

nodes.name: Other Lowtowns Gangs
nodes.legitimacy: Local/criminal/informal, varying by gang.
nodes.primary_goal: Hold territory, profit, survive under Culture primacy, and avoid becoming the kind of threat or violation The Culture must correct.
nodes.primary_fear: Culture correction, loss of territory, failed rebellion, Lyne manipulation, Council sweeps, or being made an example.
nodes.public_face: Local gangs, crews, vice operators, smugglers, enforcers.
nodes.actual_function: Territorial Lowtowns gangs that operate under the shadow of Culture supremacy.
nodes.moral_frame: Varies.
nodes.notes: Broad umbrella for Lowtowns gangs beyond The Culture. The more spatially precise node is regional_gangs, which describes the location-based gang power structures under Culture primacy.
nodes.territorial_status: Most gangs hold their own territory within Lowtowns.
nodes.relationship_to_culture: Even gangs outside Culture territory are subordinate to Culture primacy. The Culture can move through their territory, operate there, and correct them if they challenge authority or violate Culture principles/order.
nodes.historical_status: For approximately 50 years, this subordinate arrangement has been standard, with only small rebellions or adjustments that did not seriously threaten the overall structure.
nodes.relationship_to_regional_gangs: regional_gangs is the preferred spatial/territorial version of this concept.

nodes.name: Lowtowns Vice and Black Market
nodes.legitimacy: Illegal or semi-legal by Council standards; normal survival economy in Lowtowns.
nodes.primary_goal: Move goods, services, pleasures, medicine, contraband, and survival resources outside official systems.
nodes.primary_fear: Culture crackdown, Lyne capture, Council/Hightowns intervention, route disruption, or exposure into Hightowns.
nodes.public_face: Vice, smuggling, black market, street economy.
nodes.actual_function: A major Lowtowns economic system controlled or heavily shaped by The Culture; generally does not reach Hightowns cleanly or often.
nodes.moral_frame: Survival, profit, exploitation, and pleasure all mixed together. Ugly little economy with too many hands in it.
nodes.notes: Distinct from Hightowns organized crime, which is shaped/controlled by Lyne Syndicate.

nodes.name: Mines and Manufacturing Center
nodes.legitimacy: Official strategic economic interest.
nodes.primary_goal: Produce wealth, labor output, mineral/material supply, and manufacturing capacity for the city.
nodes.primary_fear: Labor disruption, sabotage, Lowtowns unrest, Culture control, Lyne conflict, or failure of extraction/manufacturing flow.
nodes.public_face: Mines, factories, industrial center.
nodes.actual_function: One of the main reasons Council/Hightowns interests directly touch Lowtowns.
nodes.moral_frame: Officially productivity and city necessity; from Lowtowns, likely exploitation and survival.
nodes.notes: A hard contact point between official power and Lowtowns.

nodes.name: Lowtowns Rent and Property Extraction
nodes.legitimacy: Legal or semi-legal property/rent system tied to Hightowns interests.
nodes.primary_goal: Extract rent and property value from Lowtowns despite administrative neglect.
nodes.primary_fear: Rent strikes, Culture interference, property damage, reform, or Lowtowns organization.
nodes.public_face: Rent, landlords, property claims, fees.
nodes.actual_function: A major expression of the broader aristocratic Lowtowns property regime: almost all Lowtowns property is officially held by aristocratic families, creating rent/property pressure across Lowtowns.
nodes.moral_frame: Officially property order; practically extraction.
nodes.notes: Connects Lowtowns poverty to Hightowns/legal property interests.
nodes.relationship_to_property_regime: Operational/economic expression of aristocratic property ownership in Lowtowns.

nodes.name: Hightowns Organized Crime
nodes.legitimacy: Unofficial and deniable; operates under or through Lyne Syndicate influence.
nodes.primary_goal: Serve elite vice, black market, corruption, and illicit needs while remaining cleanly separated from Lowtowns street systems.
nodes.primary_fear: Exposure, Lowtowns contamination, Culture encroachment, Council embarrassment, or Lyne loss of control.
nodes.public_face: Rumor, private clubs, discreet arrangements, elite favors, deniable corruption.
nodes.actual_function: Organized crime in Hightowns, controlled or shaped by Lyne Syndicate rather than The Culture.
nodes.moral_frame: Respectability with a cellar full of knives.
nodes.notes: Important distinction: Lowtowns vice/black market does not often or cleanly reach Hightowns; Lyne controls the Hightowns side.

nodes.name: The Old Boss
nodes.legitimacy: Founder of the modern Culture power structure; legitimacy rooted in war, victory, order-making, and the fifty-year settlement that followed.
nodes.primary_goal: Historically: establish Culture control over Lowtowns gangs and create a durable order.
nodes.primary_fear: N/A or historical; likely gang fragmentation, Lowtowns chaos, and failure to impose unified authority.
nodes.public_face: Founder, conqueror, organizer, old legend, or controversial order-maker depending on who tells the story.
nodes.actual_function: Created the current Culture system by going to war with the gangs for control and establishing cross-territorial Culture primacy.
nodes.moral_frame: Could be remembered as savior, tyrant, founder, criminal king, or the person who made Lowtowns livable by force.
nodes.notes: Historical node. The current Culture order is downstream of the old Boss's war against the gangs around 50 years ago.

nodes.name: The Culture's Fifty-Year Order
nodes.legitimacy: A long-standing Lowtowns power settlement maintained by force, habit, fear, utility, and Culture principles.
nodes.primary_goal: Preserve Culture primacy across Lowtowns while allowing subordinate gangs to hold territory within limits.
nodes.primary_fear: A rebellion, gang coalition, Lyne destabilization, or internal Culture failure serious enough to break the settlement.
nodes.public_face: The way Lowtowns works now: gangs have territory, but The Culture has final primacy.
nodes.actual_function: The stable power structure created after the old Boss's war, lasting approximately 50 years with only minor rebellions or adjustments.
nodes.moral_frame: Order through domination: ugly, effective, and easier to live under than constant gang war.
nodes.notes: This helps separate The Culture as an organization from the long-standing order it created.

nodes.name: Regional Gangs
nodes.legitimacy: Local territorial legitimacy varying by region, reputation, service, fear, and history; all officially accept Culture primacy.
nodes.primary_goal: Preserve territory and options under Culture primacy while watching for signs that The Boss/Culture has become weak enough to challenge or renegotiate with.
nodes.primary_fear: Committing too early, being manipulated by Lyne/Ra/outside backers, being punished by Culture, or missing the moment if The Boss falls.
nodes.public_face: Location-based gangs and local power structures across Lowtowns.
nodes.actual_function: A patchwork of territorial gangs under the thumb of The Culture. They hold local power and territory, but officially accept Culture primacy, some more reluctantly than others.
nodes.territorial_status: Each gang or crew generally anchors itself in a specific Lowtowns area, neighborhood, route, market, or industrial zone.
nodes.relationship_to_culture: All officially accept The Culture's primacy. Some do so enthusiastically, some pragmatically, some resentfully, but open refusal risks correction or destruction.
nodes.moral_frame: Varies by gang. Some may see themselves as local protectors, others as opportunists, predators, survivors, or semi-official ward bosses beneath the Culture order.
nodes.enthusiasm_for_culture_primacy: Varies. All accept it officially; not all accept it happily.
nodes.notes: Use this node for the territorial gang patchwork of Lowtowns. Individual gangs can later become child nodes.
nodes.fortnight_posture: Many regional gangs have offers or signs they may get backing, but most are not committing until they see clear Culture weakness, such as an assassination or public collapse/discrediting of The Boss. None are openly acting yet.
nodes.private_meeting_interest: A couple of gangs want a private meeting with The Boss to discuss the situation before committing.
nodes.trust_issue: All sides are hesitant due to fears of manipulation, traps, and trust issues.

nodes.name: Black Hare Society
nodes.legitimacy: Informal mercantile legitimacy in Lowtowns; illegal or semi-illegal by official Hightowns/Council standards because legitimate business is supposed to be dominated by certain Hightowns aristocrats.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain and expand Lowtowns mercantile networks, black-market trade, and economic survival systems while preserving official neutrality.
nodes.primary_fear: Being absorbed by The Culture, targeted by Lyne, crushed by Council/Hightowns business interests, losing neutral status, or having Lowtowns commerce strangled.
nodes.public_face: Lowtowns mercantile society, trade network, brokers, fixers, suppliers, and black-market business operators.
nodes.actual_function: A major Lowtowns mercantile faction that supports a decent portion of the Lowtowns economy through black-market and semi-legal trade, though not enough to make Lowtowns economically independent.
nodes.actual_alignment: Strong connections to The Culture because The Culture is the dominant Lowtowns power with the most arteries, reach, business infrastructure, and enforcement capacity.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely frames itself as practical Lowtowns survival commerce: not revolutionary independence, but keeping goods, money, and opportunities moving where official business structures exclude them.
nodes.relationship_to_culture: Officially neutral but strongly connected. This is nearly inevitable because The Culture dominates Lowtowns power, protection, routes, enforcement, and much of the criminal-economic infrastructure.
nodes.relationship_to_hightowns_business: Exists partly because official business is dominated by certain Hightowns aristocrats, leaving Lowtowns commerce to operate through black-market or semi-legal channels.
nodes.relationship_to_lowtowns_economy: Supports a meaningful part of the Lowtowns economy, but not enough to make Lowtowns economically independent from Hightowns or official extraction structures.
nodes.notes: Should be mapped as economic infrastructure rather than a gang. It is one of the arteries of Lowtowns commerce, with unavoidable Culture entanglement.

nodes.name: Satellite Spiritual Groups
nodes.legitimacy: Varies. Some are minor local extensions or sympathies of the big three; others are small independent practices with fragile legitimacy.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain small spiritual practices, local rites, minor sites, or unofficial service without becoming large enough to provoke major institutional pressure.
nodes.primary_fear: Being absorbed, suppressed, discredited, or destroyed by the major spiritual powers or ruling authorities.
nodes.public_face: Small shrines, local circles, minor practitioners, neighborhood rites, private devotional groups, tiny schools, informal sanctuaries.
nodes.actual_function: A thin spiritual ecology around and between the major powers. These are not strong networks: usually a couple of people and a few locations at most.
nodes.organizational_structure: Small, local, fragile, and rarely networked. Some are satellites of Life, Fate, or Death/Dark traditions; others are unrelated to the big three.
nodes.moral_frame: Varies wildly, which is the fun part. Some are sincere, some desperate, some weird, some old, some probably just one person and a room with bad candles.
nodes.notes: Use this as the umbrella for minor spiritual groups with weak or no network strength.

nodes.name: Unofficial Spiritual Agents
nodes.legitimacy: Unofficial; may belong to or be connected with a major power, but are not present in an officially sanctioned capacity.
nodes.primary_goal: Operate in places or situations for personal, political, spiritual, investigative, or practical reasons outside formal sanction.
nodes.primary_fear: Exposure, disavowal by their parent institution, punishment by local powers, or triggering conflict between spiritual factions.
nodes.public_face: Usually none; if seen, they may appear as ordinary travelers, minor clergy, servants, scholars, healers, or local weirdos.
nodes.actual_function: Rare unofficial presence of practitioners or spiritually connected people operating outside sanctioned institutional business.
nodes.moral_frame: Varies. Some are acting nobly, some selfishly, some because fate/life/death told them to be annoying in an alley.
nodes.notes: This is rare, but important for plot exceptions: people connected to big powers appearing where they officially should not be.

nodes.name: Unaffiliated Spiritual Entities and Practices
nodes.legitimacy: Little to none in official terms. They are not normal, not organized under the big three, and often exist in marginal or contested spaces.
nodes.primary_goal: Varies by entity or practice; survival, worship, service, hiding, feeding, teaching, haunting, blessing, bargaining, or simply existing.
nodes.primary_fear: Attention from the big three, Council suppression, elite exploitation, or being categorized as a threat.
nodes.public_face: Rumors, local saints, strange shrines, odd entities, independent practitioners, neighborhood miracles, old things nobody wants to name.
nodes.actual_function: Spiritual entities and practices not related to Fate's Paths, The Life Circle, or the Death/Dark networks. They are not common and the major powers do not make life easy for them.
nodes.moral_frame: Too varied to generalize. This is the drawer full of strange teeth.
nodes.notes: St. Aldric's is an example of this broader class or adjacent spiritual locality: not part of the big three, not normal, and existing despite institutional pressure.

nodes.name: St. Aldric's
nodes.legitimacy: Local church site of the Church of Xeneth, sustained by an old aristocratic property-use grant and Halden's long-standing missionary work.
nodes.primary_goal: Continue St. Aldric's aid/spiritual/community work despite weak resources and Halden's compromised situation.
nodes.primary_fear: Loss or renegotiation of property rights, lack of resources, local abandonment, pressure from stronger powers, and failure to attract enough active believers.
nodes.public_face: Church/local sanctuary/community spiritual site.
nodes.actual_function: The local city site of the Church of Xeneth. It survives through a property grant, limited foreign support, and Halden's practical aid to the destitute and local followers.
nodes.moral_frame: Local care and spiritual responsibility, though individual corruption or compromise can still exist.
nodes.notes: Example of a weak local spiritual site outside the big three. It is tied to the Church of Xeneth and gains influence through usefulness, aid, and Halden's presence more than formal conversion.
nodes.social_role: Aid site and local sanctuary more than a successful conversion engine. Many people come for help or listen to Xeneth ideas without officially adopting the doctrine.
nodes.local_reputation: Generally seen as helpful and useful, even by people who do not fully buy into Xeneth doctrine.
nodes.fortnight_status: Continuing its efforts under Halden despite Halden's compromised status.
nodes.halden_compromised_context: Halden has asked Xeneth for help while trying to keep St. Aldric's functioning.

nodes.name: Church of Xeneth
nodes.legitimacy: Religious legitimacy rooted in Xeneth doctrine, missionary continuity, foreign support, and an old aristocratic property grant in the city.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain and grow a humanist, soul-centered religious presence in the city while supporting believers and missionary work.
nodes.primary_fear: Loss of the St. Aldric's property grant, lack of active believers, inability to justify further resources, pressure from stronger city spiritual powers, and the possibility that local influence depends too much on Halden personally.
nodes.public_face: A small church/missionary faith in this city, larger and sometimes dominant elsewhere in the world.
nodes.actual_function: A politically weak religious institution in the city, partially supported by foreign Church of Xeneth resources and anchored locally through St. Aldric's. Its formal membership is small, and its social presence depends heavily on Halden. Halden's local entanglements may affect Xeneth's reputation without being official church connections.

doctrine.creator: Believes in one initial creator.
doctrine.mortals: Holds that mortals/souled beings are the center of creation.
doctrine.ethics: Has a system of righteousness, good, and divine justice.
doctrine.justice: Divine justice exists in a self-regulating form rather than necessarily through direct institutional enforcement.

nodes.theological_type: Humanist rather than conceptual or polytheistic.
nodes.world_presence: Exists in many places throughout the world and is dominant in some places.
nodes.city_position: Extremely weak politically within this city, with few formal believers, but possessing some soft influence through Halden's aid work and St. Aldric's usefulness.
nodes.moral_frame: Humanist and soul-centered: mortals matter, righteousness matters, and creation is morally structured around souled beings.
nodes.relationship_to_big_three: Not part of the city's dominant conceptual/polytheistic spiritual order. Weaker and more foreign in local terms, which makes it easier for the big powers to ignore, pressure, or marginalize.
nodes.notes: Important contrast faith: less conceptual-force politics, more creator/mortal/righteousness theology. In the city it survives as a weak mission rather than a major power.
nodes.local_influence_model: Low formal conversion, moderate soft influence. People may accept help, listen, and occasionally assist without committing to Xeneth's ideal of good for goodness' sake.
nodes.position_on_halden_lyne_connection: The official Church of Xeneth would likely not recognize, honor, or consider Halden's Lyne entanglement an institutional connection. It would probably treat it as Halden's local compromise, coercion, mistake, or practical entanglement rather than church policy.
nodes.local_representation_problem: Halden is effectively the church's local face, so even a personal connection can reflect on Xeneth locally despite not being official.
nodes.halden_help_request: Has received or is meant to receive Halden's message saying he is compromised and asking for help.
nodes.possible_fortnight_response: Unresolved: send aid, send investigators, disavow him, recall him, ignore him, or provide limited resources.

nodes.name: Halden
nodes.legitimacy: Long-standing missionary legitimacy through the Church of Xeneth and local service at St. Aldric's.
nodes.primary_goal: Sustain St. Aldric's, help the destitute and local followers, continue its efforts, and secure help from Xeneth after admitting he is compromised.
nodes.primary_fear: Being unable to keep the mission alive, losing property support, failing the local community, being abandoned or disavowed by the wider church, or having his compromised status exploited before help arrives.
nodes.public_face: Local missionary/priest at St. Aldric's.
nodes.actual_function: The main local representative of Xeneth's weak city presence. He mainly deals with the destitute and some followers. Few people officially subscribe to his doctrine, but many come for help, listen to his ideas, and sometimes help in return.
nodes.moral_frame: Xeneth humanist righteousness: mortals/souled beings matter, goodness matters, and justice is built into creation.
nodes.relationship_to_church_of_xeneth: Long-standing missionary tied to the Church of Xeneth, dependent on wider church support. Because he is the local representative, his actions affect Xeneth's local presence, but not every local entanglement is institutionally recognized by Xeneth.
nodes.notes: Halden remains focused on continuing St. Aldric's work. During the fortnight, he has sent word to Xeneth that he is compromised and has asked for help.
nodes.social_influence: Halden has more influence than formal believer counts suggest. His idealism and freely helping fellow mortals is a hard sell in Lowtowns, but he is seen as generally helpful and useful, so people orbit his work without fully committing to Xeneth doctrine.
nodes.formal_believer_base: Small. Few people would officially say they subscribe to Xeneth doctrine.
nodes.informal_support_base: Broader than the formal believer base. Includes the destitute, recipients of aid, sympathetic locals, occasional helpers, and people who listen without converting.
nodes.relationship_to_lyne: A real but ambiguous Lowtowns-situation link to the Lyne Syndicate. This link belongs to Halden personally/practically, not to the official Church of Xeneth. Because Lyne is not usually public knowledge, the connection is especially dangerous: Halden cannot easily explain it without revealing, implicating himself, or sounding like he is inventing a shadow conspiracy.
nodes.institutional_disavowal_risk: The official Church of Xeneth would likely not honor, endorse, or consider Halden's Lyne connection a real institutional connection. However, because Halden represents the church locally, the distinction may be invisible or irrelevant to Lowtowns observers.
nodes.lyne_exposure_risk: Very high. Since Lyne is mostly secret/deniable, exposure of Halden's link could look like corruption, betrayal, madness, or collaboration with an invisible enemy, depending on who hears it.
nodes.fortnight_status: Compromised; has sent a message to Xeneth admitting he is compromised and asking for help.
nodes.fortnight_goal: Continue the efforts of St. Aldric's despite being compromised and needing outside help.

nodes.name: Xeneth Property Grant
nodes.legitimacy: Old aristocratic will granting property use to the Church of Xeneth in perpetuity.
nodes.primary_goal: Allow the Church of Xeneth to continue using the property as originally willed.
nodes.primary_fear: Cancellation, renegotiation, legal challenge, family pressure, or neglect by the current property-holding family.
nodes.public_face: Old legal/religious property arrangement.
nodes.actual_function: The legal reason Xeneth still has a foothold in this city despite weak local political power.
nodes.moral_frame: A dead aristocrat's conversion turned into a legal-spiritual obligation his descendants do not all value.
nodes.notes: Some members of the aristocrat's family still follow Xeneth, but property-holding members provide no additional resources, and some family members want to cancel or renegotiate the arrangement.

nodes.name: Halden-Lyne Exposure Risk
nodes.legitimacy: None; this is a vulnerability created by secret entanglement.
nodes.primary_goal: N/A
nodes.primary_fear: Exposure of Halden's Lyne connection in a context where Lyne is hard to publicly explain or prove.
nodes.public_face: None until exposed.
nodes.actual_function: A dangerous pressure point: Halden's secret link to a mostly unknown/deniable syndicate can be used to compromise him, discredit him, or fracture trust in St. Aldric's.
nodes.moral_frame: The trap where doing desperate local survival things makes you look guilty even if the full system is uglier than your choices.
nodes.notes: Useful plot-pressure node. This is not a faction; it is a vulnerability created by Lyne's secrecy and Halden's representative role.

nodes.name: Lesser Aristocratic Houses
nodes.legitimacy: Aristocratic family status, property ownership, inheritance, and official legal recognition.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain family property, status, rents, business privileges, and upward access to greater elite influence.
nodes.primary_fear: Loss of property income, Founder Society exclusion, Lowtowns unrest, debt, scandal, reform, or being swallowed by stronger houses.
nodes.public_face: Lesser noble/aristocratic families, property holders, minor patrons, old names without Founder-level dominance.
nodes.actual_function: A broad layer of aristocratic families below the Founder Society. They are not the apex, but collectively hold major property interests, especially in Lowtowns.
nodes.moral_frame: Likely frames ownership as inheritance, duty, lawful property, or family survival.
nodes.relationship_to_founder_society: Subordinate to or excluded from the Founder Society, though some houses may aspire to sit at the table or become useful to founding families.
nodes.relationship_to_lowtowns: Many lesser houses hold Lowtowns property and benefit from rents/extraction, creating pressure on Lowtowns even when they lack Founder-level power.
nodes.notes: This node prevents 'Founder Society' from accidentally meaning all aristocrats. The aristocracy has layers.

nodes.name: Aristocratic Lowtowns Property Regime
nodes.legitimacy: Official legal property system: almost all Lowtowns property is held by aristocratic families.
nodes.primary_goal: Maintain aristocratic ownership of Lowtowns property and extract value through rent, legal claims, and property control.
nodes.primary_fear: Lowtowns tenant organization, property reform, rent refusal, Culture interference, Lyne exposure, Council embarrassment, or aristocratic legal challenges.
nodes.public_face: Landlords, deeds, rents, property law, leases, inherited claims, management agents.
nodes.actual_function: A structural pressure system on Lowtowns: most property is officially held by aristocratic families, meaning Lowtowns residents live under external ownership and extraction.
nodes.moral_frame: Officially lawful ownership and civic order; materially an extraction and pressure system on Lowtowns.
nodes.relationship_to_lowtowns: Applies constant pressure because residents, businesses, and local institutions often operate on land/property owned by distant aristocratic families.
nodes.relationship_to_founder_society: Founder families are the most powerful owners, but the regime also includes many lesser aristocratic houses.
nodes.notes: This should probably appear as a broad structural overlay rather than a simple faction node. It pressures Lowtowns continuously.

nodes.name: Lyne Lowtowns Shadow Operatives
nodes.legitimacy: None publicly; covert authority derives from Lyne Syndicate backing, secrecy, money, blackmail, and access to Hightowns interests.
nodes.primary_goal: Operate inside Lowtowns on behalf of Lyne Syndicate while remaining unknown, deniable, and difficult to distinguish from ordinary Lowtowns instability.
nodes.primary_fear: Exposure by The Culture, Lowtowns locals, rival gangs, Halden/St. Aldric's fallout, or any event that clearly reveals Lyne's hand.
nodes.public_face: Usually none. May appear as locals, informants, small criminals, merchants, desperate workers, clerks, fixers, religious contacts, or gang-adjacent nobodies.
nodes.actual_function: Mostly unknown covert operatives and assets in Lowtowns used by Lyne Syndicate to influence, destabilize, gather intelligence, move money, and manipulate events.
nodes.moral_frame: The city is easier to control when the hand doing the pushing is invisible.
nodes.relationship_to_lowtowns: Embedded inside Lowtowns but mostly unknown; their work contributes to instability without making Lyne legible as the cause.
nodes.relationship_to_the_culture: Potentially dangerous to The Culture because they can seed conflict, compromise local actors, and make instability look organic.
nodes.notes: This node should be visually hidden or semi-transparent in ordinary map views. It exists for reader/author truth, not public knowledge.

nodes.name: The Workmen
nodes.legitimacy: Informal legitimacy rooted in skilled labor, technical knowledge, stable earnings, and essential industrial work. Usually viewed more as a labor resource/class than a faction.
nodes.primary_goal: Historically, to maintain work, stability, crew ties, and technical usefulness. During the first-day/fortnight period, increasingly to help each other find work, barter, arrange support, and build community/self-improvement networks.
nodes.primary_fear: Becoming visible as a political labor faction, provoking Hightowns retaliation, losing work, being divided, or having their emerging community organization crushed before it matures.
nodes.public_face: Workers, technicians, crews, shop-floor specialists, miners, mechanics, builders, factory hands, resource-extraction labor, and practical industrial experts.
nodes.actual_function: Usually does not behave like a faction; more often functions as a labor/technical resource class within Lowtowns and Hightowns-linked industry. However, around first_day and fortnight, Workmen begin organizing around a community concept: helping each other find work around Lowtowns, barter/arrangements, self-improvement, and consistent mutual support.
nodes.historical_status: Historically dominated by Hightowns business interests and aristocratic property/capital power. Past attempts at direct opposition or negotiation with Hightowns have generally not ended well for them.
nodes.class_position: A significant part of Lowtowns' population with somewhat stable earnings, making them materially distinct from the most destitute Lowtowns groups while still subordinated to Hightowns interests.
nodes.organization_status: Baseline: not usually a faction and not strongly organized politically. First-day/fortnight: beginning to form a more consistent, unofficial community network focused on mutual aid, work-finding, bartering, arrangements, and self-improvement. Not currently framed as direct opposition to, or negotiation with, Hightowns.
nodes.moral_frame: Practical labor dignity and survival: help each other get work, improve, and endure without openly becoming the kind of political threat Hightowns historically punishes.
nodes.relationship_to_lowtowns: Part of Lowtowns and one of its more stable earning populations. During first-day/fortnight, beginning to create a consistent unofficial community support network.
nodes.relationship_to_hightowns: Historically dominated by Hightowns business/property interests. The current emerging organization avoids direct opposition or negotiation with Hightowns because such things have historically ended badly.
nodes.relationship_to_founder_society: Founder/aristocratic business interests benefit from Workmen labor. They are not usually focused on suppressing Workmen organization unless it becomes overtly political, threatening production/property, or resembles direct labor challenge.
nodes.relationship_to_lyne: Lyne may watch or influence them if needed, but baseline Workmen are more resource/class than faction. Risk increases if their community organization becomes a platform for broader Lowtowns coordination.
nodes.notes: Do not over-map the Workmen as a normal faction in pre-story baseline. They become faction-like only as an emerging first-day/fortnight community network.

focus: helping each other find work around Lowtowns
emerging_first_day_fortnight_structure.historical_reason_for_caution: Historically, direct opposition or negotiation with Hightowns has not ended well for Workmen.

nodes.culture_alignment_pressure: The Culture wants the Workmen to become more formally linked to Culture and more focused on Lowtowns interests than on serving Hightowns business systems.
nodes.jon_role: Jon, Gren's father, is the informal center of the emerging Workmen community network, though he claims not to run it.

nodes.name: Workmen Emerging Community Network
nodes.legitimacy: Informal legitimacy based on mutual usefulness, work-finding, bartering, self-improvement, and community support among Workmen.
nodes.primary_goal: Build practical cooperation among Workmen for Lowtowns benefit while preserving neutrality and avoiding capture-prone leadership dependency.
nodes.primary_fear: Being captured by a faction, becoming too formal and targetable, remaining too informal to negotiate/protect itself, or collapsing if Jon is eliminated.
nodes.public_face: Informal mutual aid, work referrals, bartering arrangements, self-improvement, and community organization among workers/techs.
nodes.actual_function: The first-day/fortnight-era organization emerging among Workmen. It is not official and not directly oppositional, but it is becoming consistent enough to matter. Jon is its informal center while denying leadership; his deeper concern is making the network resilient beyond any single person.
nodes.moral_frame: Practical neutrality and mutual problem-solving: help Workmen, help Lowtowns, avoid becoming someone else's weapon.
nodes.relationship_to_workmen: Emerges from the Workmen class/resource base but is not identical to all Workmen.
nodes.relationship_to_hightowns: Avoids direct opposition or negotiation because historical attempts have not ended well.
nodes.notes: The key rub is not that Jon is dreaming. The rub is designing distributed representation that can still make agreements.
nodes.lyne_fortnight_threat: During the fortnight, Lyne actively aims to destabilize this burgeoning guild/community structure before it becomes resilient or politically meaningful.
nodes.culture_alignment_pressure: The Culture may try to pull this emerging Workmen network into a more formal Culture-linked Lowtowns structure.
nodes.leadership_model: No formal structure by Jon's preference; Jon claims he is not running it. This creates a representation problem as the network becomes more consistent and others want agreements with it.
nodes.neutrality_goal: Remain neutral in the sense of not being captured by Culture, Hightowns, Lyne, Founders, or any official faction. Neutrality does not necessarily rule out formal links or agreements.
nodes.cultural_goal: Develop a cultural belief among Workmen in working together and solving problems together.
nodes.benefit_scope: Benefit Workmen directly, but with all of Lowtowns in mind in a practical way.
nodes.technology_concern: Ensure the new technology invented during the fortnight section is used properly and not dangerously.
nodes.formal_link_problem: The network can be neutral and formally linked, but it cannot make durable formal ties without some recognized decision method. Jon resists person-based representation because one representative or council can be killed, corrupted, extorted, or captured.
nodes.representation_problem: The Workmen need distributed or culture-based representation: enough structure to coordinate, but not so much that one person or group becomes the kill/corrupt/extort point.
nodes.anti_capture_design_need: The emerging network needs a way to make decisions and agreements that is resilient if Jon, a delegate, or a local group is removed or compromised. Jon's expected removal makes this urgent, not theoretical.
nodes.jon_removal_risk: Jon believes he will be targeted and likely eliminated soon, so the network needs to survive without him.

nodes.name: Lyne First-Night Lowtowns Operation
nodes.legitimacy: None publicly; covert Lyne operation.
nodes.primary_goal: Watch the Workmen's emerging organization and actively weaken The Culture during the first night.
nodes.primary_fear: Exposure, Culture counteraction, Workmen noticing the pattern, or Lowtowns actors realizing Lyne is the hidden source of pressure.
nodes.public_face: None. Effects appear as local tension, coincidence, gang instability, labor unease, or Culture weakness.
nodes.actual_function: A first-night Lyne operation focused on monitoring Workmen emergence and weakening Culture primacy.
nodes.moral_frame: Keep the hand invisible while the structure bends.
nodes.notes: Time-scoped operation for first night. This should be filterable separately from Lyne's enduring strategic goals.

nodes.name: Lyne Fortnight Lowtowns Operation
nodes.legitimacy: None publicly; covert Lyne operation.
nodes.primary_goal: Destabilize the Workmen's burgeoning guild/community structure and severely destabilize or destroy The Culture.
nodes.primary_fear: The Workmen network becomes resilient, The Culture survives and identifies Lyne's hand, The Boss becomes a martyr, weaker gangs fail to destabilize the order, or Lyne loses deniability.
nodes.public_face: None. Effects appear as gang opportunism, Culture leadership crisis, resource scarcity, rumors, internal fractures, and Workmen disorganization.
nodes.actual_function: A fortnight-era Lyne campaign to fracture Lowtowns stabilizing structures by targeting The Culture's leadership/resources and undermining the Workmen's emerging organization.
nodes.moral_frame: Break the local stabilizers before they become politically real.
nodes.notes: Fortnight operation. Escalates from first-night surveillance/weakening into an active destabilization campaign.
nodes.regional_gang_context: Lyne's support of weaker gangs operates in an environment where most gangs are hesitant and waiting for clear Culture weakness before open commitment.

nodes.name: The Boss
nodes.legitimacy: Leader of The Culture; legitimacy tied to Culture authority, strength, order, and inheritance of the fifty-year structure.
nodes.primary_goal: Keep her father's legacy alive, keep The Culture going, and preserve Culture dominance in Lowtowns.
nodes.primary_fear: Failing her father's legacy, losing Culture dominance, assassination, discrediting, internal fracture, Lyne manipulation, gang rebellion, or inability to protect Lowtowns from Hightowns aggression.
nodes.public_face: The head of The Culture.
nodes.actual_function: Personal leadership node for The Culture. She embodies the current continuation of her father's legacy and the Culture's dominance. During the fortnight, Lyne and Ra both target her because Culture stability is bound up in her survival and credibility.
nodes.moral_frame: Preserve the legacy, preserve the order, keep Lowtowns from being swallowed.
nodes.relationship_to_the_culture: Leader and symbolic center of The Culture's current power.
nodes.notes: The Boss's personal aim is inseparable from Culture continuity: keep her father's legacy, keep the Culture alive, keep it dominant.
nodes.legacy_pressure: Her core personal/political burden is preserving her father's legacy and the Culture order he created or passed down.
nodes.regional_gang_fortnight_pressure: Some regional gangs are waiting for clear weakness before acting, while a couple seek private meetings. Her survival and perceived strength are key to keeping them from committing against Culture.

nodes.name: Egasdaniste
nodes.legitimacy: Personal wealth, major J'h'ell business ownership, foreign leverage, reputation, private networks, and the practical reality that his individual power behaves like an institution.
nodes.primary_goal: Expand influence through lending, law, and ideology; identify structural weaknesses; push the City toward debt primacy; and secure partial or full adoption of his worldview through laws, institutions, or aligned movements.
nodes.primary_fear: Misreading the City's power structure, being blocked by Founders or Lyne, failing to legalize stronger debt enforcement, religious rejection, overextension, or a social structure too resistant to debt-based hierarchy.
nodes.public_face: One of the richer people in J'h'ell: a powerful foreign businessman whose personal resources and influence make him function like a faction or foreign power.
nodes.actual_function: A single individual whose wealth, business holdings, foreign reach, and lending capacity are large enough to be mapped as a faction/foreign power. He is personally inseparable from the factional shell called the Bank of Egas.
nodes.moral_frame: Debt is not just money to him; it is relation, merit, hierarchy, obligation, and afterlife structure. A society with many losers and few winners may read to him as morally legible rather than cruel.
nodes.relationship_to_bank_of_egas: The Bank of Egas is not a real bank and not a normal institution; it is the factional/political shape of Egasdaniste's personal wealth, lending power, and foreign influence.
nodes.notes: Egasdaniste's full social transformation is aspirational, but he is not all-or-nothing. He can profit and advance his worldview through partial institutional capture: a law here, a debt court there, a movement of hungry little believers with ledgers.
nodes.business_position: One of the richer people in J'h'ell and owner of various businesses.
nodes.foreign_expansion_goal: Seeking to expand his influence in foreign territories, including this city.
nodes.spiritual_affiliation: Unofficial adherent to an Ell-based religion centered on an afterlife structure based on debt relations to other souls.
nodes.spiritual_role: Not just a money/political node: also a spiritual node through his unofficial adherence to debt-afterlife religion.
nodes.fortnight_goal: Meet with Lyne and the Founder Society; understand the City’s sociopolitical and economic structure and weaknesses; begin the institution of a legally recognized and more thoroughly enforced debt system in both Hightowns and Lowtowns.
nodes.long_term_goal: Ultimate horizon: restructure the City's society toward a system aligned with his worldview: steep meritocracy with many losers and few winners, a legal structure giving debt much stronger primacy in execution, and conversion of as many people as possible into the Ell-based debt-afterlife religion. He recognizes this may not fully succeed, so incremental legal and ideological footholds are acceptable wins.
nodes.ideological_project: Debt, meritocracy, social sorting, legal enforcement, and religious conversion are not separate projects for Egasdaniste. They reinforce each other as one worldview.
nodes.success_model: Egasdaniste knows his ultimate debt-meritocracy/religious restructuring may not fully succeed. Partial victories still matter: a few stronger debt laws, legal recognition of debt primacy, or the creation of a new faction/movement aligned with his values would count as a win.

nodes.name: Bank of Egas
nodes.legitimacy: A practical fiction built around Egasdaniste's personal wealth, J'h'ell business holdings, lending capacity, and foreign influence. Called a bank, but not a real bank.
nodes.primary_goal: Extend Egasdaniste's influence in foreign territories through loans, deals, business expansion, legal debt structures, and religiously inflected debt ideology.
nodes.primary_fear: Being mistaken for a normal bank or formal institution; losing coherence if separated from Egasdaniste personally.
nodes.public_face: A named foreign financial/power interest associated with Egasdaniste.
nodes.actual_function: Not a real bank. A single-man power structure: the political, financial, lending, legal-debt, spiritual, and foreign-power footprint of Egasdaniste.
nodes.institutional_reality: Not a real bank. Not meaningfully separable from Egasdaniste as a person.
nodes.moral_frame: A man large enough that the world has to invent a desk for him.
nodes.relationship_to_egasdaniste: Embodies Egasdaniste's factional power. Without him, it may not exist in any meaningful institutional sense.
nodes.notes: Use this node when the map needs to show Egasdaniste as a lender/faction/foreign power rather than only as a character.
nodes.relationship_to_founder_society: The Founder Society is debating borrowing money from Egas and wants to meet him.
nodes.relationship_to_lyne: Lyne wants to borrow money from Egas.
nodes.fortnight_goal: Serve as the practical shell for Egasdaniste's meetings with Lyne and the Founder Society and the opening push toward stronger legal debt recognition/enforcement.
nodes.long_term_goal: Function as the vehicle for Egasdaniste's debt-based restructuring of the City: stronger debt law, enforceable obligations, social hierarchy, and religious conversion.

nodes.name: J'h'ell Business Interests
nodes.legitimacy: Foreign business ownership, wealth, trade, and private influence rooted in J'h'ell.
nodes.primary_goal: Expand business reach and influence into foreign territories.
nodes.primary_fear: Foreign political barriers, debt failure, reputational loss, overextension, or local power blocs resisting entry.
nodes.public_face: Foreign businesses, investors, merchants, lenders, and private power brokers.
nodes.actual_function: The foreign business base from which Egasdaniste draws wealth and influence.
nodes.moral_frame: Expansion through business, debt, and private leverage.
nodes.notes: Placeholder for Egasdaniste's J'h'ell economic base.

nodes.name: Ell Debt-Afterlife Religion
nodes.legitimacy: Spiritual legitimacy among adherents; unofficial in Egasdaniste's case.
